title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Client Candor - Past False Testimony
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A client informs their paralegal that they lied on the witness stand during a hearing the previous week to make their damages look worse than they were. The adjudicator has not yet rendered a decision. What is the paralegal's **first action**?
options: Immediately inform the adjudicator that the client committed perjury.
Advise the client that they must correct the false testimony, and if they refuse, the paralegal must withdraw.
Keep the information confidential and hope the adjudicator does not notice.
Offer to testify on the client's behalf to clarify the misunderstanding.
questions.explain: When a paralegal discovers that a tribunal has been misled by their client, the paralegal must advise the client of their moral and legal obligation to disclose the truth to the tribunal. If the client refuses to consent to the disclosure, the paralegal *must* withdraw from the representation (mandatory withdrawal) under Rule 8.02. The paralegal cannot directly disclose the perjury to the tribunal without the client's consent due to confidentiality rules.
